hints: Focus on what alkaline iodine is really testing for, the yellow precipitate of iodoform and the special groups that can form it.
Remember the two families that give a positive result are ethanal and methyl ketones with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, plus ethanol and methyl secondary alcohols with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.
Check each pair for one molecule that contains one of those methyl groups and one that does not, because that pair will give one yellow precipitate and one with no change.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Great, let us start with the big idea. Alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ is the iodoform test. A positive result is a pale yellow precipitate of triiodomethane.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3(s) + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Learn the two positive groups**

Two structures give this yellow solid. One is the ethanoyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, found in ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and methyl ketones ($\text{CH}_3\text{COR}$). The other is the related alcohol group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, found in ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) because it is first oxidised to ethanal in situ.

**Test each pair for same or different**

Now apply it. Ethanol and ethanal are both positive, so same result. Ethanal and propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) are both positive, so same result. Ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and pentan-3-one ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5$) are both negative, as acids do not react and the ketone has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so same result.

**Find the mixed pair**

Ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it gives the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate. Propanal ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it stays as brown iodine solution with no precipitate. One positive and one negative means a different visible result.

options.A: Both give a positive result, so the visible result is the same. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ under the conditions, and $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so both form yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
options.B: Both give a positive result, so the visible result is the same. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ is ethanal and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ is a methyl ketone, both contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group needed for iodoform formation.
options.C: Both give a negative result, so the visible result is the same (no precipitate). $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ does not give iodoform despite having a $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ unit, and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5$ is not a methyl ketone so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.D: This pair gives different results. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ gives a positive test with yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate, while $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$ (propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group and gives a negative test with no precipitate.
